about: slapstic page 2 $8E00-$93FF: the wave 1 probots - the orbit state, the change between universe and player-relative position, the animation of the leg points, the per-frame view of the five records at ALIEN (body, legs, head, the lazar aim test, the launch of transmissions and shots), the probot shot down, then a dead copy of TIE fighter set-up code and of SNVW left from an earlier build

P2:8E1D.name: probot_do_orbit
P2:8E1D.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 10 (entry 10 of the handler table P2_8873): turns the probot around the point in words $15 and $17 of its record, which P2_8DD2 picked. U = the probot record. makes the position player-relative, multiplies the offset from the point by $0800 or -$0800 (matrix program MS_PERS), the sign taken from the head angle (byte $10), and takes the y product off x and adds the x product to y, a small rotation about the point. it never picks a new behaviour itself

P2:8E54.name: probot_pos_rel
P2:8E54.desc: makes the position of the probot at U player-relative: when bit $08 of byte 0 is set it clears the bit and takes the player's position (s1_tx, s1_ty) off the x and y words at 5 and 7. does nothing when the position is relative already. called first by nearly every state routine

P2:8E6D.name: probot_pos_abs
P2:8E6D.desc: the reverse of P2_8E54: when bit $08 of byte 0 of the record at U is clear it sets the bit and adds the player's position (s1_tx, s1_ty) to the x and y words at 5 and 7, so the probot holds a place in the universe. called by the fixed place state (P2_89F0) and when a probot is shot down

P2:8E86.name: probot_legs_anim
P2:8E86.desc: animates the legs of the probots by moving the points of objects 9-$10 in math RAM, from w1_anim_pts to w1_anim_end: eight legs of four 8-byte points, whose spare bytes 6 and 7 serve as a timer and a mode. for each leg, bytes 6 and 7 of point 0 count a random time of up to $70 calls and hold a random mode: 0 moves points 1, 2 and 3, $01 moves points 2 and 3, $80 or $81 moves point 3 alone. the first point moved has its own timer (up to $3F calls) and a random direction 0-7 that picks the move routine from the table at P2_8F1F, and the same routine is run for every point moved. point 0, the root at the body, never moves. called by P2_877C once for every live probot in a frame, and all probots draw the same points. X and U are preserved

P2:8F2F.name: leg_pt_ydn_xup
P2:8F2F.desc: leg point move 7 of the table at P2_8F1F: y one step down (P2_8F7C), then falls into P2_8F31 for x one step up. X = the point

P2:8F31.name: leg_pt_x_up
P2:8F31.desc: leg point move 0 of the table at P2_8F1F: raises by 1 the x offset of the point at X from the point before it (8 bytes back) and stores x again as the previous point's x plus the offset, so a point follows the one before it. an offset that passes $20 is held at $20 and the direction is reversed (P2_8F93)

P2:8F48.name: leg_pt_xy_up
P2:8F48.desc: leg point move 2 of the table at P2_8F1F: x one step up (P2_8F31), then falls into P2_8F4A for y one step up. X = the point

P2:8F4A.name: leg_pt_y_up
P2:8F4A.desc: leg point move 1 of the table at P2_8F1F: as P2_8F31 for the y word of the point at X (offset 2), its offset from the previous point's y raised by 1 and held at $20

P2:8F61.name: leg_pt_yup_xdn
P2:8F61.desc: leg point move 3 of the table at P2_8F1F: y one step up (P2_8F4A), then falls into P2_8F63 for x one step down. X = the point

P2:8F63.name: leg_pt_x_dn
P2:8F63.desc: leg point move 4 of the table at P2_8F1F: lowers by 1 the x offset of the point at X from the point before it and stores x as the previous point's x plus the offset. an offset below -$20 is held at -$20 and the direction is reversed (P2_8F93)

P2:8F7A.name: leg_pt_xy_dn
P2:8F7A.desc: leg point move 6 of the table at P2_8F1F: x one step down (P2_8F63), then falls into P2_8F7C for y one step down. X = the point

P2:8F7C.name: leg_pt_y_dn
P2:8F7C.desc: leg point move 5 of the table at P2_8F1F: as P2_8F63 for the y word of the point at X (offset 2), its offset from the previous point's y lowered by 1 and held at -$20

P2:8F93.name: leg_pt_reverse
P2:8F93.desc: flips bit 3 of byte 7 of the point at X, which turns each of the eight move directions into its opposite (0 and 4, 1 and 5, 2 and 6, 3 and 7). called by a move routine when the point's offset reaches its limit. the byte is that of the point being moved, so for the second and third point of a run it is not the byte the direction was read from

P2:8F9A.name: probot_timers
P2:8F9A.desc: counts down the two timers of the probot at U, each until it is 0: byte 3, the time to the next shot, and byte $14, the time to the next transmission. called by P2_877C every frame for every live probot. the frame counter is masked with 0 before each count, so both count every frame

P2:8FB7.name: probots_view
P2:8FB7.desc: view of the wave 1 probots, called from bank 0 through maze entry MZ_8196 by vew_probot, vew_probot_end, vew_probot_die and the training manual's man_view_probot. for each of the five $1A-byte records from ALIEN up to xmit_atst it sets S2_PRM to the record, clears the per-frame flags in byte 1 and, when the record is live, views the probot (P2_8FD3). Y = the display list

P2:8FD3.name: probot_view
P2:8FD3.desc: views the probot at U. its position (words 5, 7 and the height at 9, with the player's position added when it is held player-relative) goes through matrix program MS_PSB2 into the player's view, and the result is kept in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT. the probot is left out when its depth is $0100 or less or $3C00 or more, or when it is outside the 45 degree pyramid on either side or up and down. otherwise bit $10 of byte 1 is set (in view), bit $80 is set when it is near enough to the middle of the screen from side to side, the test that allows a transmission, and the body, the colour of the head and the head are drawn (P2_909A, P2_9080, P2_90FD)

P2:9080.name: probot_xmit_col
P2:9080.desc: writes the colour word $67C0 to the display list ahead of the head when the probot at U is about to transmit: transmission timer (byte $14) under 4, prog_count under 4 and bit $04 of byte 0 set. otherwise the head is drawn in the colour of the body

P2:909A.name: probot_draw_body
P2:909A.desc: draws the legs and body of the probot whose record is in S2_PRM. sets the ship 2 block to unit vectors (UNITV), yaws it by the body spin angle (byte 11) and concatenates it with the player's view (MS_CNCT). then the legs (P2_91CC), colour $62C0, the points of object 4 and of object 5 raised by the bob offset (P2_90CC), the draw routine those two objects share, the beam back to the centre (bank 1 KD8AC) and the lazar aim test on the body (P2_9272). leaves U = the record

P2:90CC.name: probot_neck_pts
P2:90CC.desc: moves the centre used for the next object points up the probot's own axis by the bob offset (word 13 of the record at U): the point 0, 0, offset goes through matrix program MS_PAD and the result replaces M_XT, M_YT and M_ZT. then processes the points of object 5 (JOBJBPNT), the ring the head sits on. the head drawn afterwards uses the same raised centre

P2:90FD.name: probot_draw_head
P2:90FD.desc: draws the head of the probot at U. yaws the ship 2 block by the head angle (byte $10) on top of the body spin and concatenates it again, processes the points of object 6 and draws it, runs the lazar aim test on the head (P2_92B0) and the launches (P2_9125), then draws object 7, which uses the points of object 6 and comes out in the colour P2_9125 set, and returns the beam to the centre

P2:9125.name: probot_head_acts
P2:9125.desc: writes colour $6480 for the last part of the head, puts the universe position of the probot at U (words 5, 7 and 9, the player's position added when it is held player-relative) in M_XT2, M_YT2 and M_ZT2 as the place a transmission or a shot starts from, and tries both launches (P2_9158). X and U are preserved

P2:9158.name: probot_launch
P2:9158.desc: tries to launch a transmission (P2_9175) and then a shot (P2_915F) from the probot at U, whose depth is in M_XT and whose universe position is in M_XT2, M_YT2, M_ZT2. called when the head is drawn and once more when the probot is shot down

P2:915F.name: probot_try_shot
P2:915F.desc: lets the probot at U fire at the player: when its depth M_XT is above $0400, bit $02 of byte 0 is set and the shot timer (byte 3) has run out, it calls page 1 P1_9063, which reloads the timer and may start a shot from the position in M_XT2, M_YT2, M_ZT2

P2:9175.name: probot_try_xmit
P2:9175.desc: lets the probot at U send a transmission: when its depth M_XT is above $0400 and under $3000, prog_count is under 4, bit $04 of byte 0 is set, bit $80 of byte 1 is set (near the middle of the screen) and the transmission timer (byte $14) has run out, it calls page 3 P3_98E8, which starts a transmission at the position in M_XT2, M_YT2, M_ZT2 and returns carry set when a record was free. then the bob direction (byte 15) is set to $FF, downwards, and the timer is loaded again (P2_91A8)

P2:91A8.name: probot_xmit_delay
P2:91A8.desc: loads the transmission timer (byte $14) of the probot at U: the entry of the table at P2_91C3 for w1_pace (8 at most), plus a random part of the same entry, plus 4. the entries fall from $3F to 2, so the probots transmit more often as the pace rises. X is changed

P2:91CC.name: probot_draw_legs
P2:91CC.desc: draws the legs of the probot at U: one of objects 9-$10 for each bit set in the part mask (byte $13), bit 0 for object 9. the four points of the leg are processed (JOBJBPNT) and the width of 6 units at the probot's depth is worked out with the divider and MS_PERS. the leg is drawn down from the body with the draw routine of object 9 and BJ_CX moved by that width, then back up with the draw routine of object 10 and BJ_CX moved the other way, so the two passes lie one width either side of the points and meet at the tip. a width of 2 or less gives a single line. the beam returns to the centre after each leg

P2:9233.name: lz_oct_dist
P2:9233.desc: distance on the screen from the lazar cursor (LZ_CX, LZ_CY) to the perspected point at X (x word, y word), by the octagon rule the Star Wars collision tests use in line: the larger of the bigger axis distance and 9/16 of the sum of the two. returns it in D less 10, not below 0. uses tmp_scal and the temp at $4803

P2:9272.name: probot_body_aim
P2:9272.desc: lazar aim test on the body of the probot at U, after its points are processed. when the probot's depth M_XT is less than the depth of the nearest probot found so far (prb_aim_dep) and the cursor is within the size of 45 units at that depth from point 18 of object 4, the middle of the body (P2_9233), it records this probot in prb_aim_rec and its depth in prb_aim_dep. page 3 P3_9838 reads them when the lazars fire

P2:92B0.name: probot_head_aim
P2:92B0.desc: lazar aim test on the head of the probot at U: the same as P2_9272 with a size of 30 units and point 19 of object 6, the middle of the head

P2:92EE.name: probot_shot_down
P2:92EE.desc: the probot in prb_aim_rec is hit by the lazars: jumped to from page 3 P3_9838 through maze entry P3_8454 when a probot is under the cursor and its depth is less than the one in $4C09, the next thing P3_9838 compares. the first time in a game it sends speech command $05 (foa_said). it makes the probot's position absolute, starts an explosion there (bank 1 BGBKXP through L6198), scores 25 points while bonus_left is not 0 and 250 after, sends sound $4E, gives the probot a last try at a transmission and a shot (P2_9158) and frees the record. while bonus_left is not 0 it is counted down, and the kill that brings it to 0 scores 5,000, awards the Jedi letter (page 1 P1_9573) and raises quota_probot by one

5098.name: s1_tx
5098.desc: MS_TX+M_S1: the player's universe x position, word, first of the position words $5098/s1_ty/s1_tz. the pages add it to and take it off an object's x to change between universe and player-relative coordinates

4CAF.name: w1_anim_pts
4CAF.desc: word: math RAM address (BJ_RAM) taken by the probot set-up after objects 4-7 are loaded, so the first of the 8-byte point records of objects 9-$10. P2_8E86 starts its per-frame point animation here

4CB1.name: w1_anim_end
4CB1.desc: word: math RAM address (BJ_RAM) taken by the probot set-up after object $10 is loaded, the end of the point records that P2_8E86 animates

4CB3.name: leg_obj
4CB3.desc: temp of P2_91CC: the object number, 9-$10, of the probot leg that goes with the mask bit being looked at

4CB4.name: leg_mask
4CB4.desc: temp of P2_91CC: the probot's part mask (byte $13 of its record), shifted right one bit for each leg until it is 0

507E.name: leg_width
507E.desc: word in math RAM, temp of P2_91CC: the width of 6 units at the probot's depth, 0 when it comes to 2 or less. BJ_CX is moved by it so that the two passes along a leg lie one width either side of its points

4C0D.name: prb_aim_dep
4C0D.desc: word: view depth of the nearest probot whose body or head the lazar cursor is on this frame, set with prb_aim_rec by P2_9272 and P2_92B0. page 3 stores $FF in its high byte each frame (P3_95C3) for none, and P3_9838 compares it with the depths of the other things under the cursor to decide what the lazars hit. P2_92EE reads it back as the depth of the probot shot down

4C0F.name: prb_aim_rec
4C0F.desc: word: address of the record of the probot whose depth is in prb_aim_dep. P2_92EE takes the probot that is shot down from here

questions: P2:934B-93D1 - the 135 bytes shown as data are code, but dead code. linear decoding gives 934C STA WV_LVL, 934E LDX #ALIEN / LDU #M_AL / LDB #MS_ALBC and the loop that gives each alien record its unit vector block, 936D JSR $9ACC, 9370 RTS, then from 9371 a second routine that runs the same loop, makes alien 0 live, faces it towards the player at x $1000, stores #$9C56 in word 13 of the record, JSR $9A1A, loads object 0 (the TIE fighter) through L60A8 and returns at 93D1. the same two routines are live on page 3 at P3_85EC and P3_8613 (there with JSR P3_8D85, #$908B and JSR NWCHOR_P3). on page 2 nothing reaches the block: the tracer has no reference to 934C, 934E or 9371, no maze entry leads there (the only operand that points into it, JSR P2_93B4 at P2_85B9, is a decoy), and its own calls to $9ACC and $9A1A land in the middle of instructions of page 2. the byte before it tells what it is: the routine began LDA #$00 / STA WV_LVL at $934A, and the present P2_92EE ends with its RTS on $934A, over the $86, leaving the operand $00 at $934B. so it is the tail of an earlier build of this ROM that the shorter final code did not overwrite. it could be listed as code under a header that says so, the starts being 934C (first instruction cut), and 9371

P2:9361-9561 - pages 2 and 3 hold the same bytes over this whole range (byte compare of the two pages), which takes in the end of the dead block above and SNVW at P2_93D2 and S2VW at P2_93E9 with what follows them. on page 2 SNVW has no caller (the tracer lists it as an orphan entry) and S2VW is called only from SNVW, so this copy of the two Star Wars routines is as dead as the block before it. bank 0 views the TIE fighters through page 3 SNVW_P3, and page 3 lists this same copy as P3_9371 (no caller found) and SNVW_P3_2. the carried names and comments are right for the code, so they are left alone here

P2:8E86 - the routine is called inside the per-record loop of P2_877C, once for each live probot, although it animates the one shared set of leg points. so the legs move faster the more probots are alive. described as the code runs

P2:8F93 - the reverse bit is flipped in byte 7 of the point being moved. for the first point of a run that is the byte its direction is read from, for the points after it it is their own byte 7, which is the direction byte of a shorter run (or, for no point, the mode byte, since point 0 never moves). whether Atari meant that is not clear

P2:903F - the lined up test uses PH_TIM: factor $80 (any probot on the screen passes) at 300 or more, $C0 at 150-299, and under 150 $C0 from w1_level 2 up and $FF (within half the depth of the middle) below. I did not check in bank 0 which way PH_TIM runs in the probot phases, so the comments give the numbers only

P2:909A / P2:90FD - yaw_by_angle is run on block index 9 twice between one UNITV, first with the body spin angle and then with the head angle, each followed by MS_CNCT. I took the second yaw as added to the first (the head turns on the spinning body) and did not verify in the matrix processor program that MS_CNCT leaves block 9 turned

P2:90C2 - L60E4 (bank 1 KDA2C) draws the object whose number is still in BJ_ID, which is 5 after P2_90CC. the draw table KD6CD has the same routine KBA37 for objects 4 and 5, and the point start table KD77C puts object 5's points right after object 4's 19 points ($4E05 and $4E64), so I describe one routine drawing both. I did not read KBA37 to its end

P2:8684 / P2:915F / P2:9175 - byte 0 of a probot record as this stretch uses it: 0 free, bit $02 may shoot, bit $04 may transmit, bit $08 position is in universe coordinates. bits $01 and $10 (the manual's table has $01 and $11) are not tested in this stretch
4803 - P2_9233 uses the temp at $4803 under two of its Star Wars names in the same routine (CMPD TMPSIZ, then bare $4803). it has six aliases in the defines already, so no new name is given
5098 4CAF 4CB1 - named here with the names p2_8a00.json (s1_tx) and p2_85ec.json (w1_anim_pts, w1_anim_end) gave them, same text, so that the listing of this stretch shows them
